contexts.tariff_increase: 2026/27 (from 1 Jul 2026): 6.67% overall; commercial/industrial large users: LV 7.75-9.01%, MV 8.27-9.62%, HV 8.43-9.17% depending on component; residential energy charge 8.55%.
contexts.reliability: Best of the three metros: Steenbras 180MW pumped storage protects City customers from up to ~2 stages of Eskom load-shedding (IPP programme aims for 4). Eskom-supplied areas (Khayelitsha) do not benefit.
contexts.sseg_rules: Must apply for City authorisation before installation (online). Bi-directional meter at customer's cost. Cash for Power: commercial payouts monthly once credit > R5,000; commercial feed-in 82.06c/kWh + 25c/kWh incentive (incentive retained for 2026/27). Wheeling permitted within City network with deficit energy tariff; wheeling from City-network generators to customers outside network not permitted. Unauthorised systems: R6,425.90 disconnection/reconnection fee reported.
contexts.verify_how: City bill or prepaid token (City of Cape Town vending); City/Eskom supply-area query: power@capetown.gov.za or SMS 31220; City load-shedding area lookup (City vs Eskom schedule).

Registration turnaround reported 3-6 weeks. Tshwane pursuing 1,000MW IPP procurement; no confirmed operational wheeling framework found.

contexts.tariff_increase: 2026/27 (from 1 Jul 2026): 8.63% average; ~9.01% for business, LPU and commercial reseller tariffs. 2025/26 was 12.41% average, with business fixed/capacity charges +18.32% and energy +13.32%.
contexts.reliability: Frequent substation/transformer failures and cable theft in southern Soweto (e.g. Pimville Zone 9 outage Jan 2026; 13-day Kliptown outage 2022). No load reduction regime like Eskom's, but ageing network.
contexts.sseg_rules: SSEG must be registered with City Power; registration requires migration to a time-of-use tariff with fixed monthly charges (reported ~R1,094 capacity + R271 service). Feed-in tariff (~R0.86/kWh announced 2023) not operational as of reports - design for self-consumption. Registration turnaround reported 10-14 weeks. City of Johannesburg approved wheeling tariffs (2025/26) enabling third-party energy trading over City Power grid.
contexts.verify_how: City Power bill / prepaid token (City Power vending), City Power load-shedding suburb list (citypower.co.za 'Names of suburbs' PDF), City Power call centre 0860 562 874.

contexts.service_area: direct supply: most of Soweto, Mabopane, Ga-Rankuwa, Winterveld, parts of Soshanguve, most of Khayelitsha
contexts.tariff_increase: +8.76% for direct customers from 1 Apr 2026 (FY2027), applied across Businessrate, Miniflex, Megaflex, Nightsave Urban, WEPS, Homepower/Homelight; +9.01% to municipal bulk from 1 Jul 2026. Prior year (FY2026) was +12.74% (NERSA approved 12.7%).
contexts.reliability: No national load-shedding in 2025-26, but Eskom runs 'load reduction' in high-loss/non-payment township feeders (typically 05:00-09:00 and 17:00-22:00) - ongoing in Soweto, Mabopane, Ga-Rankuwa, Winterveld, Soshanguve in 2026. Eskom said 342,701 customers were removed from peak load reduction by 17 Apr 2026; aims to end it by 2027 via smart meters. Eskom suspended services in parts of Khayelitsha (Mar 2025) after staff hijacking. In Cape Town, Eskom areas do not get the City's Steenbras shield.
contexts.sseg_rules: All grid-tied SSEG must register with Eskom even if non-exporting. <100kVA: Eskom registration only; 100kVA-1MW: Eskom + NERSA registration. Registration/connection fee waiver (incl. free smart meter, up to R10k urban / R36k rural) for systems up to 50kVA ran to 30 Sep 2026 - check if extended again. Export credits on bill at variable energy rate (Gen-offset / Gen-purchase / Gen-wheeling tariff options exist). Eskom accepts electrician CoC + NRS 097-2-1 inverter certificate.
contexts.verify_how: Customer's bill/account number from Eskom or prepaid token receipt naming Eskom; Eskom load-shedding / load-reduction lookup by suburb (loadshedding.eskom.co.za) - if the suburb appears under Eskom direct it is Eskom-supplied; call 08600 ESKOM (08600 37566).
